problem.claim: Diffusion-bridge distribution transport methods must balance scalable training with access to optimal pairings.

gap.claim: Unsupervised matching is computationally costly, whereas fully supervised optimal pairing is often infeasible; a practical middle ground is needed.

contributions.claim: Introduces Feedback Schrödinger Bridge Matching, a semi-supervised framework using fewer than 8% pre-aligned pairs as state feedback for non-coupled samples.
Formulates semi-supervised guidance as an additional term in a static Entropic Optimal Transport objective and recasts it dynamically for scalable matching.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors characterize FSBM as a novel semi-supervised matching framework for partially aligned datasets.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments show faster training and improved generalization when coupled-pair guidance is used.
The authors report that using a small portion of pre-aligned pairs—under 8% of the dataset—significantly improves efficiency.

narrative_sequence.summary: Existing diffusion-bridge matching methods trade off scalability against access to optimal training pairings.
FSBM uses fewer than 8% pre-aligned pairs to guide transport for non-coupled samples.
The method adds semi-supervised guidance to static EOT and converts the objective to a dynamic formulation.
Experiments are reported to show accelerated training and enhanced generalization.

source_observation.claim: The abstract connects a supervision trade-off to a concrete design: a small fraction of aligned pairs provides feedback for otherwise non-coupled data.

lessons.interpretation: A resource constraint can be framed as an intermediate regime rather than a binary supervised-versus-unsupervised choice.
lessons.application: When writing a method paper, define the limiting extremes, then specify the smallest informative supervision signal and how it enters the objective.
lessons.exception: This framing is unsuitable when no reliable aligned subset exists or when partial supervision cannot be operationalized.

unknowns: No datasets, baselines, quantitative speedups, generalization metrics, or experimental conditions are specified.
The abstract does not explain how pre-aligned pairs are obtained, selected, or used during training.
The reported efficiency and generalization improvements are author claims from the abstract and are not independently verified here.
